transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

Good news: what you're describing sounds like the vacuum working as designed, not a failing motor.

## What's happening

The V15 Detect has an Auto mode that adjusts suction power on its own:

• Floor type: The cleaner head senses resistance from the brush bar. On a rug or carpet it ramps up suction to pull dust from deep in the pile, then drops back down on hard floors like tiles.
• Dust levels: A piezo sensor in the bin counts particles. When it detects more dust, it boosts power.
• Battery reading: The screen shows estimated runtime at the current power level. When suction goes up, the estimate drops; when it goes down, the estimate recovers. It's recalculating, not losing charge abnormally.
• Moving display: The bar graph shows particle counts in real time, so it's meant to rise and fall as you clean.

## How to check

Press the mode button (above the screen) to switch from Auto to Eco. In Eco the power stays fixed, so you shouldn't hear the change between tiles and rug. If it then behaves consistently, everything is fine.

## Signs of a real problem worth reporting

• Pulsing (power surging on and off rhythmically): usually a blockage or a dirty filter, sometimes a battery fault
• Cutting out unexpectedly, or not lasting near its rated runtime even in Eco
• Burning smell, grinding or rattling noises
• Error messages or flashing lights on the screen
• The brush bar not spinning

If you notice any of those, contact Dyson support while you're under guarantee. Even if you're just unsure, they're generally happy to talk you through it, and it's worth having a record on file. But from what you've described, your vacuum is simply working harder on the rug, which is exactly what it's supposed to do.

Thank you, I've just tried that. In Eco it stays the same quiet sound on both the rug and the tiles. There's also no burning smell, heat or warning lights at any point. Does that mean it's definitely nothing to worry about?

Yes, that's a very reassuring result. Staying steady in Eco but changing in Auto shows the power shifts come from the vacuum's sensors deliberately adjusting suction, not from a fault. A failing motor wouldn't politely stay constant in one mode and only vary in another. Together with no smell, heat or warning lights, there's nothing here that points to a problem.

I can't inspect the machine, so I wouldn't promise it will never develop a fault, but there's no sign of one now and nothing to report.

## Keeping it in good shape

• Wash the filter about once a month in cold water only (no detergent), and let it dry fully for at least 24 hours before refitting.
• Clear the brush bar of tangled hair now and then.
• Empty the bin before it reaches the MAX line.
• Use Eco or Auto for everyday cleaning to get longer runtime, and save Boost for stubborn spots.

## Worth knowing for the future

Under your guarantee, keep an eye out for runtime that drops noticeably over time (even in Eco), pulsing, cutting out, or error messages on the screen. If any of those appear, contact Dyson then. For now, your V15 is just doing its job.
